title: It was not the first battery-saved game.
description:
It was not the first battery-saved game. The Legend of Zelda, 1986, is officially the first game with a battery as part of the cartridge. That wording is precise because it has to be.

An obscure Super Cassette Vision game that used a battery backup a year before Zelda. Nintendo itself had used the concept even earlier, in a 1984 programming add-on.

It made the battery disappear. Earlier battery-backed cartridges needed players to load their own bulky AA batteries. Zelda hid a slim button cell inside a cartridge that looked completely ordinary, saving up to three files.

That one hidden battery helped kill Nintendo's own disk drive.
